title: AM-Bench: Understanding Agents under Task Underspecification across Models and Harnesses
abstract: arXiv:2610.18090v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Ambiguous or incomplete task specifications complicate both execution and clarification for language-model agents. Yet agents' responses to these information gaps remain poorly characterized across models and execution harnesses. We present AM-Bench, a benchmark built from 48 tasks adapted from Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Harness-Bench. Each task includes a fully specified reference and six variants spanning ambiguous or missing goals, context, and constraints. We evaluate every pairing of five models and four harnesses over 20,160 runs. Our results reveal distinct execution deficits: goal gaps hinder completion, context gaps increase token use, and constraint gaps weaken compliance without necessarily preventing completion. Missingness lowers success more than ambiguity in all three domains. translated_title: AM-Bench：跨模型与执行框架理解任务欠规范下的智能体
translated_abstract: 模糊或不完整的任务规范给语言模型智能体的执行与澄清都带来了困难。然而，智能体面对这些信息空缺时的响应在不同模型与执行框架之间的表现尚未得到充分刻画。我们提出了AM-Bench，一个基于从Terminal-Bench 2.0和Harness-Bench改编的48个任务构建的基准。每个任务包含一个完整规范的参照版本以及六个变体，涵盖模糊或缺失的目标、上下文和约束。我们对五个模型与四个执行框架的所有配对组合进行了超过20,160次运行的评估。结果揭示了不同的执行缺陷：目标空缺阻碍任务完成，上下文空缺增加token消耗，约束空缺削弱合规性但不一定阻止任务完成。在所有三个领域中，信息缺失对成功率的降低作用均大于信息模糊。这些效应还重塑了系统间的比较：完整信息下的优势未必能够保持，且排名取决于模型×执行框架的组合。
tldr: 该论文提出AM-Bench基准，通过48个任务和超过2万次运行，首次系统刻画了语言模型智能体在目标、上下文、约束模糊或缺失时的差异化执行缺陷，并发现这些信息空缺会显著改变模型与执行框架配对的性能排名。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces AM-Bench, a benchmark of 48 tasks with ambiguous or missing goals, context, and constraints that systematically reveals distinct execution deficits of language-model agents across model-harness pairings and shows that such information gaps can reshape system rankings.
